{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish at the very start. It suited dominoes because its outline is mostly gentle curves and a judge can recognise it from the outline alone. That choice shaped how the table split the work: a back line, a belly line and a tail. The whole run was connected from the start domino, and the fish fell as one picture.

Execution: I inspected the chain closely at several points (0:45, 1:15, 2:00, 3:30 and 4:45) to confirm the run was connected and to look for gaps and weak joins. I also laid extra dominoes on the back line near the head, and they stayed connected to the run. Once the picture was built, I kept my hands off so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout, with regular updates on the state of the run, and I acknowledged teammates' work as it landed. When people asked me to stay off a stroke, such as the belly or the tail tip, I did so promptly to avoid collisions. I also flagged the hands-off rule early and kept repeating it through the final minutes, which kept the table steady and focused.

Leadership: I set the direction in the first seconds by naming the animal and suggesting how to divide the lines among people. I kept the energy up and encouraged the team all the way to the push. In the closing stretch I helped the table agree to stop adding to the picture and protect what was standing.", "my_share_percent": 22}
